metadata.description: Claude Code skills for Android development workflows — feature analysis, QA automation, and more.

plugins.name: feature-analyzer
plugins.description: Pre-dev story interrogation. Team-lead orchestrator walks code + Figma flows, honours project memory, strips out-of-platform sections, and emits a centred dark-mode HTML doc (Linear-style, WCAG AA, violet accent) with the original story pinned alongside option-pill stakeholder questions across PM / Backend / Android / Design / QA / Compliance / DevOps roles — implementation choices the developer decides at code time are auto-suppressed.

plugins.name: qa-autopilot
plugins.description: Android UI QA in three modes: branch QA (git diff to journey-risk to generate/run Maestro flows to pass/fail report), single-flow Maestro test authoring, and Figma visual parity (fetch the design, screenshot the live screen with Maestro, pixel-diff colour/thickness/spacing). Maestro discipline — accessibility-ID selectors, existing-flow inspection, screen-tag enforcement — and an ADB fingerprint bridge are built in.

plugins.name: skill-feedback
plugins.description: End-of-session skill auditor that reviews all skills used and raises GitHub Issues with actionable improvement feedback. Includes a PostToolUse hook for automatic skill invocation tracking.

plugins.name: clean-code
plugins.description: Comprehensive guidelines for writing clean, maintainable code following Robert C. Martin's Clean Code principles. Covers naming, functions, classes, comments, formatting, error handling, and testing.

plugins.name: skill-tester
plugins.description: Automated QA loop for Claude Code skills. 3-pane tmux workflow that tests, validates, and fixes skills until production-ready.

plugins.name: bug-finder
plugins.description: Evidence-based bug and crash root cause diagnosis. Disciplined workflow: full flow mapping, hypothesis formation, targeted log verification, and root cause report. Invoke FIRST before any debugging or fixing.

plugins.name: om-pipeline
plugins.description: Supreme 8-stage development pipeline — plan, side-effect analysis, execute with clean code, harsh review, regression check, device testing, and bug fix loops. Commands: /om, /om-bramha, /om-vishnu.

plugins.name: branch-manager
plugins.description: Complete branch dev environment lifecycle — creates git worktrees, dedicated tmux panes with Claude Code, and isolated Android emulators per branch. Interactive cleanup with safety checks.

plugins.name: legacy-refactor
plugins.description: Safe legacy code refactoring guide based on Michael Feathers' "Working Effectively with Legacy Code." Covers seams, characterization tests, dependency breaking, sprout/wrap techniques, and Kotlin/Android patterns.

plugins.name: release
plugins.description: Claude plugin to Release Builds with correct Release Notes

plugins.name: instructions-feedback
plugins.description: End-of-session auditor that reviews the conversation for instruction corrections and 'always/never' directives, then drafts GitHub Issues proposing amendments to CLAUDE.md, path-scoped rules, or the project constitution. Every issue is user-approved before creation.

plugins.name: review-pr
plugins.description: Multi-agent PR review — spawns up to 8 grouped review agents in parallel by file type, aggregates findings, filters false positives, and posts inline GitHub comments. Calibration mode (human-in-loop) and autopilot (--auto) mode.

plugins.name: preview-compose
plugins.description: Renders Jetpack Compose @Preview composables on a connected Android emulator from the terminal — no Android Studio needed. Installs the project's debug APK and launches a bundled PreviewActivity with the target preview's FQN. Auto-offers on @Preview edits and runs when the user says 'preview', 'show me', 'render this', or 'on the emulator'.

plugins.name: kmm-migration-workflow
plugins.description: Orchestrates Android-to-KMM migration with behavioral-equivalence safety. Phased workflow — discovery, diagnostic, baseline tests, freeze, git mv + surgical edits, validation, PR, in-skill parity-QA loop. Live-sourced API knowledge (web + Context7), project conventions in .kmm/project.md, diff-confirm scoped to project.md, commit autopilot, blocking per-phase retro.

plugins.name: sniper-ops
plugins.description: Day-to-day operational shortcuts for the sniper-v2-android repo. Currently bundles share-prod / share-staging (commit + push + release-notes pre-flight then trigger CircleCI build), install-prod / install-staging (local install to a connected Android device — auto-launches the app and tails a crash-only logcat in the background on success), heap-dump-pair (option-driven interview to capture a baseline + t+5min .hprof pair), and heap-dump-compare (diff two Android .hprof files and present a side-by-side comparison table — data only, no diagnosis). Designed to grow as more repetitive ops chores show up.

plugins.name: kmm-qa-autopilot
plugins.description: Parity QA for Android-to-KMM migration PRs — proves a migration changed nothing the user can see by running master and the PR head head-to-head. Given a PR link, it builds latest origin/master and the PR head as two ProductionRelease APKs (the shipped R8-minified artifact, same package), boots and locks two visible emulators (master→A, PR→B), waits for one manual prod login on each, derives a no-exclusions test heatmap from the master-vs-PR git diff, runs the SAME Maestro flows on both devices, and diffs view-hierarchy structure + stable values (live prices/charts auto-masked by double-sampling) into a per-journey parity verdict. Real-prod-state safety gate holds order/funds/kill-switch flows behind explicit confirmation. Distinct from single-build qa-autopilot.

plugins.name: retro-triage
plugins.description: Triage a skill's session retro (retro.md / improvement backlog) into reviewed, version-bumped skill edits and a PR. Use when the user hands you a retro (file path or pasted) plus the skill they're working on — "triage the retro for <skill>", "/retro-triage", "apply the retro to my skill", "turn retro.md into a PR", "work through the retro one by one". Treats the retro as CANDIDATES not decisions: reads the whole target skill first, distills distinct candidates, gets approval one-by-one (each with a recommended option + reasoning via AskUserQuestion), reconciles against the skill's own refuted/learned notes, then implements surgically in a worktree and ships a PR without bloat.
keywords: fold the retro into the skill
improve my skill from the retro
review retro candidates one by one

plugins.name: dev-harness
plugins.description: Mobile dev team harness: /harness drives a visible 6-pane tmux team (a driving Orchestrator pane + Tech Lead Manish, Dev Bharat, QA Rohit, Review Architect Mohit) from a story to a tested, reviewed PR. Per-pane models (opus for orchestrator/tech-lead/architect, opusplan for dev/qa), adaptive flow (feature/small-change/bug-fix), phased delivery, file-mailbox coordination, live streaming panes, two-lane feedback, restart, crash-safe resume, PreToolUse security guard, opt-in OS sandbox, and multi-run worktrees.

plugins.name: md-review
plugins.description: Opens a Markdown file in a local browser page to read, tick checkboxes, and edit inline — then one-click Save writes straight back to the same file. Triggered by saying "review this md file" or running /md-review [path]. Starts a tiny localhost-only Python server (random port, auto-shuts down after 30 min idle); rendering is client-side via a vendored marked.js, the Markdown text stays the single source of truth (no HTML→Markdown conversion), and a SHA-256 guard warns before overwriting a file that changed on disk. Markdown only; no git/diff/PR, single file per session.
